headline: World Bank trims Bangladesh growth forecast to 4.6% amid global turmoil
summary: The global lender warns that economic growth in the current fiscal year could weaken further due to the fallout from the Iran war.
details: The World Bank has projected Bangladesh’s GDP growth at 4.6 percent for the next fiscal year, signaling a more cautious outlook due to mounting external pressures.
This forecast is 1.9 percentage points lower than the 6.5 percent growth target set by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury in the proposed national budget.
The bank also warned that growth in the 2025–26 fiscal year could slow further to 3.8 percent, down from its previous January projection of 4.6 percent.
The World Bank attributed this downward trend to the economic fallout from the Iran war, which is expected to weigh on the global economy.
Globally, worldwide growth is projected to drop to 2.5 percent in 2026—the weakest level since the COVID-19 pandemic.
For South Asia, the growth forecast has been revised down to 6.3 percent for 2026, compared to 7 percent in 2025.
The World Bank's outlook remains below the provisional estimates provided by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS).
The official government target had been revised down from 6.75 percent to 5.25 percent before the interim administration's budget of 5.5 percent.
caption:
Bangladesh's economic growth forecast has been slashed by the World Bank. Global turmoil and the Iran war are taking a toll.

The World Bank has projected Bangladesh’s GDP growth at 4.6 percent for the next fiscal year, signaling a more cautious outlook due to mounting external pressures.

This forecast is 1.9 percentage points lower than the 6.5 percent growth target set by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury in the proposed national budget.

The bank also warned that growth in the 2025–26 fiscal year could slow further to 3.8 percent, down from its previous January projection of 4.6 percent.

The World Bank attributed this downward trend to the economic fallout from the Iran war, which is expected to weigh on the global economy.

Globally, worldwide growth is projected to drop to 2.5 percent in 2026—the weakest level since the COVID-19 pandemic.

For South Asia, the growth forecast has been revised down to 6.3 percent for 2026, compared to 7 percent in 2025.

The World Bank's outlook remains below the provisional estimates provided by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS).

The official government target had been revised down from 6.75 percent to 5.25 percent before the interim administration's budget of 5.5 percent.

headline: 14 injured as bus overturns on Dhaka-Mawa Expressway
summary: The accident occurred after the driver lost control of the vehicle, leaving several passengers injured.
details: A bus overturned on the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway, leaving 14 people injured.
The accident happened when the driver lost control of the vehicle, causing it to flip over on the highway.
Emergency responders and security personnel arrived at the scene to assist the victims and manage traffic.
The injured passengers have been shifted for medical treatment following the crash.
caption:
